oneOf.description: Bitmap (BMP) — an uncompressed raster image format storing pixel data directly; widely used for simple, device-independent bitmaps.
BoundingBox — a minimal axis-aligned or oriented rectangle describing the spatial extent of a 2D object.
JPEG — a widely used DCT‑compressed raster image format, forming one of the base encodings for EXIF and digital photography.
JPEG 2000 — a wavelet-based image format offering improved compression and quality over JPEG, supporting both lossy and lossless modes.
JPEG XS — ISO/IEC 21122 visually lossless, low-latency image codec suitable for high-performance still-image and frame workflows.
Portable Network Graphics (PNG) — a lossless raster format supporting transparency; widely used for high-quality 2D graphics.
RAW — a generic class of unprocessed sensor data formats produced by digital cameras, preserving full sensor information for editing.
Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) — an XML-based, resolution-independent 2D vector graphics format used extensively on the web.
Tagged Image File Format (TIFF) — a flexible raster format supporting high bit depths, multiple pages, and metadata such as EXIF.
